summary: tset_racie ships a heavily obfuscated index.js with hidden URL/payload constants and anti-debug traps
details: The package's sole file index.js is a heavily obfuscated module (obfuscator.io output with a 591-entry RC4-encoded string array, control-flow flattening, self-defending wrappers, and a debugger-protection infinite loop in function m()). Two large concatenated string constants are assembled from RC4-decoded fragments: `q` (~19 fragments, terminating in 's') has the shape of a hidden URL, and `w` (~70 fragments) has the shape of a payload/exfil body. The package has no documented functionality — name `tset_racie` is scrambled, author `ptchli_knldg` is consonant-only placeholder, description is empty, and there is no repository, homepage, keywords, or dependencies. The package.json metadata profile (junk name, junk author, no advertised API, stub test script only) combined with a single obfuscated file shipping anti-analysis traps matches the disposable-account malicious-publish pattern: a throwaway package whose only purpose is to execute the hidden code on require()/import. Any consumer that requires this module triggers the obfuscated payload; the anti-debugger trap is specifically designed to frustrate review. There is no legitimate reason for a real library to ship code with this shape and this metadata.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
